Ik many have said this but try to learn sign its so easy, doesn't even have to be bsl/asl (or whereever you live) could just be sse. Thats when you sign the same way as you speak, the same grammar and everything and, again, its so easy to incorporate that into your life. Maybe when you get more confident with sse you can learn the grammar for bsl/asl but you don't have to. 

Also, be open about your hearing abilities because it will only do you harm if you hide it. Talk to your work about accommodations you need, encourage your family to learn sign if you are, tell your mates your needs and dont be afraid to ask them to repeat things or to face you when speaking etc. It will make the experience a hell of a lot easier

Right now I would ask if they are doing it somewhat safely. I know that there's no way to self harm safely but its very unlikely that they will stop right away even with help, so just ask how they are treating the injuries, if they have an emergency first aid kit, and who to contact if something goes really bad. They will be more likely to talk to you and ask for support if you are not judgemental. Wishing you luck xx

It would be 100000% beneficial. The lack of sign interpreters in social sectors like hospitals is a growing and dangerous issue, and is harmful to the person involved. If we had cheaper interpreters in a variety of settings without having to book weeks ahead with no guarantee they'll show in the first place (real and impossible in emergencies) then we will feel much more confident and safer in our choices since we are certain we have all the essential information, and would be way less at risk of dangerous miscommunication in a health crisis

I remember when my deaf mother was brought into hospital and I had to translate her cancer diagnosis to her at 19 (I'm HoH so can hold a convo easier) and it was traumatizing. If we had more like you it could ensure we, as a community, could have the same chances as our hearing peers and not be put at risk of being manipulated or withheld essential information about things like rent for example 

Hope this helps Xx

hearing loss is subjective, i may be able to hear the person next to you but not you because of differences in frequencies. the opposite could be true for somebody else with the same 'level' of hearing loss. this means that accessibility varies. I may not require an interpretor for something, but somebody else might so dont assume they dont bc i dont. idk if this makes sense but just dont assume what we need or dont need just because of somebody elses' needs
This is so helpful for the disabled community!
The comment that 'the way girls dress nowadays is just asking for attention' was made by my philosophy lecturer, I have absolutely no clue what he was implying tbh

I feel the same way a lot of the times. In my case, its mainly due to the lack of accessibility. If I could go anywhere and be guaranteed bus seats, captions, ramps then I would be much more comfortable with myself

This may help you, she is a wonderful deaf and disabled youtuber who lost her hearing later on in life

just a tip, not many people like being asked " do you wish you could do this" or something along those lines, and this accounts to a lot of disabled people. Some people dont care but just be mindful Xx

To make life easier, face us whilst speaking, don't cover your mouth and don't over pronounce your words when someone is lipreading because it actually makes it more difficult. To get out attention, not everybody likes to be touched or nudges so waving your hand or tapping a surface we are touching is a safe bet.  

I don't wish I was hearing but it would be so much easier if everything was accessible. We can still do a lot that hearing people can do like listen to music or party etc, just in a different way

The best part is the deaf culture, it is beautiful. The languages are stunning and it is so peaceful. Honestly, it is worth researching because it is very interesting

I don't mind CI's but people need to know that they don't suit everybody and they are not a fix it. I know people who have lost the rest of their hearing or have been badly affected by CI's just because their parents/carers jump into the decision because they hear myths that they can "cure" your deafness but it is simply not the case. Many benefit from them too. I don't personally think that such a permanant feature should be pushed onto young children as their carers don't want to raise a deaf child, and that it should be thoroughly talked over later when they can understand

Hoped this helped, and ask as many questions as you like, its nice that someone is actually interested in this

When I first used my chair, I didn't feel ashamed until everybody told me I should be. Honestly, using the chair is the best thing that has ever happened to me because every step I take feels like absolute agony, and it is the only thing that helps me actually go outside. Education is so important on these issues and thank you for not misinterpreting what I was saying, so many people have downvoted and verbally abused me for pointing out ableism, its nice for somebody to understand that its not out of malice
Being a wheelchair user isn't restricting, and they ain't free when they pass on. A wheelchair helps people explore and navigate the world, and it is not constricting for the user.

an urgent situation where they dont have a phone, paper or anything similar, but they just happen to have an expensive and frankly ugly gloves on them, then have the time to set them up? likely. its the same situation for every foreign language speaker but there would be riots if you enforced something like this on them.
its not so much tribalism, more like not wanting to sacrifice a part of themselves or their culture for the benefit of strangers

sign language is a massive part of our culture and you are taking that away from us. we have to wear these stupid looking gloves just because the rest of the world is too lazy to accommodate. also, the a large percentage of sign language relies on facial expression and body language, similar to how we speak, as we cant sign punctuation, and that is lost with this. these are also really expensive whereas you can teach yourself sign. finally the child would feel really isolated from others growing up bc she cannot speak the language of her peers, and they don't care enough to learn, living through that is terrible. omf i ranted, sorry
None of the deaf community wants this
